logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, with current or previous symptoms, use of 1 of the 3 beta blockers proven to reduce mortality (bisoprolol, carvedilol, sustained-release metoprolol succinate) is recommended to reduce mortality and hospitalizations.

source_text: In patients with HFrEF, with current or previous symptoms, use of 1 of the 3 beta blockers proven to reduce mortality (eg, bisoprolol, carvedilol, sustained-release metoprolol succinate) is recommended to reduce mortality and hospitalizations.

logic_node.action_detail: Only bisoprolol, sustained-release metoprolol succinate, and carvedilol have been shown to reduce mortality in HFrEF. The favorable findings should not be considered a beta-blocker class effect. Other beta blockers (e.g., nebivolol, bucindolol) are not included in this recommendation.

source_text: The favorable findings with these 3 agents, however, should not be considered a beta-blocker class effect in HFrEF. Other beta blockers are not included in this recommendation for use.

logic_node.action: Initiate bisoprolol at low dose and titrate to target
logic_node.action_detail: Bisoprolol: starting dose 1.25 mg once daily, target dose 10 mg once daily. Mean dose achieved in clinical trials was 8.6 mg total daily.

source_text: Bisoprolol | 1.25 mg once daily | 10 mg once daily | 8.6 mg total daily

logic_node.action: Initiate carvedilol at low dose and titrate to target
logic_node.action_detail: Carvedilol: starting dose 3.125 mg twice daily, target dose 25-50 mg twice daily (25 mg BID standard, 50 mg BID if >85 kg). Mean dose achieved in clinical trials was 37 mg total daily.

source_text: Carvedilol | 3.125 mg twice daily | 25-50 mg twice daily | 37 mg total daily

logic_node.action: Initiate carvedilol CR at low dose and titrate to target
logic_node.action_detail: Carvedilol CR (controlled-release): starting dose 10 mg once daily, target dose 80 mg once daily.

source_text: Carvedilol CR | 10 mg once daily | 80 mg once daily

logic_node.action: Initiate metoprolol succinate ER at low dose and titrate to target
logic_node.action_detail: Metoprolol succinate extended release (metoprolol CR/XL): starting dose 12.5-25 mg once daily, target dose 200 mg once daily. Mean dose achieved in clinical trials was 159 mg total daily.

source_text: Metoprolol succinate extended release (metoprolol CR/XL) | 12.5-25 mg once daily | 200 mg once daily | 159 mg total daily

logic_node.action: Titrate beta blocker to target dose
logic_node.action_detail: Beta blockers should be initiated at low doses, and every effort should be made to achieve the target doses shown to be effective in major clinical trials, as tolerated. Even if symptoms or LVEF improve, long-term treatment with target doses should be maintained.

source_text: Beta blockers should be initiated at low doses, and every effort should be made to achieve the target doses of the beta blockers shown to be effective in major clinical trials, as tolerated.

logic_node.action: Initiate beta blocker before discharge if clinically stable
logic_node.action_detail: Beta blockers can be safely initiated before hospital discharge, provided patients are clinically stabilized and do not require intravenous inotropic therapy for HF. Beta blockers should be prescribed to all patients when HFrEF is diagnosed, including in-hospital, unless contraindicated or not tolerated.

source_text: Data show that beta blockers can be safely initiated before hospital discharge, provided patients are clinically stabilized and do not require intravenous inotropic therapy for HF.

logic_node.action_detail: Abrupt withdrawal of beta-blocker therapy can lead to clinical deterioration and should be avoided unless indicated. Even if symptoms or LVEF improve, long-term treatment should be maintained to reduce the risk of progression in LV dysfunction or major cardiovascular events.

source_text: Abrupt withdrawal of beta-blocker therapy can lead to clinical deterioration and should be avoided unless indicated.

logic_node.action: Continue beta blocker even if asymptomatic or LVEF improves
logic_node.action_detail: Even when asymptomatic, or when symptoms are mild or improve with other therapies, beta-blocker therapy is important and should not be delayed until symptoms return or disease progression is documented. Even if symptoms or LVEF improve, long-term treatment with beta blockers and use of target doses should be maintained.

source_text: Even when asymptomatic, or when symptoms are mild or improve with other therapies, beta-blocker therapy is important and should not be delayed until symptoms return or disease progression is documented.

logic_node.action: Reattempt beta blocker after contraindication resolves
logic_node.action_detail: If a contraindication or intolerance to beta-blocker therapy is noted, they should be documented, and the patient restarted on beta-blocker therapy in the future, so long as an absolute contraindication is not present.

source_text: If a contraindication or intolerance are noted, they should be documented, and the patient restarted on beta-blocker therapy in the future, so long as an absolute contraindication is not present.

logic_node.action: Recognize limited beta-blocker benefit in atrial fibrillation
logic_node.action_detail: Benefits of beta blockers in HFrEF were observed in patients with or without CAD, diabetes, older patients, women, and across racial and ethnic groups, but NOT in patients with atrial fibrillation.

source_text: These benefits of beta blockers were observed in patients with or without CAD, and in patients with or without diabetes, older patients, as well as in women and across racial and ethnic groups but not in patients with AF.
